correctness.rationale: Two distinct blocks meet in at most one point, yielding the stated four distance classes and the block-block term 4^p J+(2^p-4^p)N^T N+((k-1)4^p-k2^p)I. Full row rank of N and b>v give a nonzero zero-sum block kernel, which is positive above p*=log2(k/(k-1)) and zero at it. On the mean-zero paired modes the endpoint determinant is (r-1)(a^2/(k-1)-(3^p*-1)^2), with a=k/(k-1); for k>=4 the mean-value theorem bounds 3^p*-1 by (log2 3)a/(k-1), and for k=3 one has (3/2)^(5/3)<2 and 1< (3/2)/sqrt(2). The first diagonal entry is negative. On the constant-population zero-sum mode the form normalized by vb is -rv-2v(b-r)(3^p*-(2^p*+4^p*)/2), strictly negative by concavity. The orthogonal splitting exhausts the zero-sum form, proving the endpoint equality space exactly. Strict negative type below follows from the Schoenberg nesting result, and rank of the centered Gram gives both least affine dimensions. Standalone finite diagnostics starting with graph distances independently reproduced the inertias for AG(2,3), PG(3,2), and AG(2,5).
residual_risks: Floating-point inertia checks are finite diagnostics; the exact endpoint sign and nullity follow from the analytic argument.
